title: UEC European Road Championships 2026 preview: Routes, favourites and how to watch

UEC European Road Championships 2026 preview: Routes, favourites and how to watch

The 2026 UEC European Championships will take place from Friday 2nd to Wednesday 7th October 2026 in Ljubljana, Slovenia, not even a week after the World Championships. It reverses the programme from Montreal, kicking things off with the road races and ending with a full day dedicated to all the individual time-trials.

The course is hilly, with the circuit used across the races repeating the Možjanca climb, which features gradients up to almost 16% – perfect for Slovenian native Tadej Pogačar, if he hadn’t ended his season early.

Last year, the elite road races were won by Pogačar and Demi Vollering with time-trial victories going to Remco Evenepoel and Marlen Reusser. The U23 road races were won by Jarno Widar and Paula Blasim while Jonathan Vervenne (Belgium) and Federica Venturelli (Italy) won the TT. Karl Herzog (Germany) and Michiel Mouris (Netherlands) won the junior men’s road race and time-trial respectively and Paula Ostiz (Spain) doubled up in the junior women’s events. France’s elite sextet topped the standings in the mixed relay ahead of Italy while Norway took home the gold in the junior field.

UEC European Road Championships 2026 key information

  • Dates: Friday 2nd – Wednesday 7th October 2026
  • Location: Ljubljana, Slovenia
  • TV coverage: HBO Max, Eurosport, YouTube

UEC European Road Championships 2026 routes

U23 Women Road Race, 88.4km

All the road races take place on or finish on a 22.1km circuit around Šenčur, 14 miles north of Ljubljana. The circuit features 367m of elevation via the big climb to Možjanca, which comes after 5km and has a maximum gradient of 15.8%. The U23 women will cover four laps to total 88.4km and 1,616m of elevation.

U23 Men Road Race, 141.9km

The U23 men’s peloton will begin in the centre of Ljubljana and head northwest towards Škofja Loka over a flat parcours, crossing the Sava river south of Kranj to arrive at the Šenčur circuit. They will take on three laps for a total of 1,698m of elevation over 141.9km.

Junior Men Road Race, 110.5km

It’s five laps of the circuit with no dillydallying for the junior men, amassing 2,020m of elevation gain over 110.5km.

Elite Women Road Race, 130km

For the elite women, the race begins in Ljubljana for 85.8km of leg-softening prior to their arrival at the Šenčur circuit. They’ll complete just two laps over a short 130km, with 1,359m of elevation.

Junior Women Road Race, 66.3km

Three laps await the junior women, totalling 66.3km and 1,212m of elevation.

Elite Men Road Race, 196.3km

Just like the U23 men and elite women, the elite men will depart from Ljubljana and cover 85.8km before taking on five laps of the circuit. Over 196.3km the elevation gain totals 2,571m, so expect tired legs by the end.

Junior and Elite Mixed Relay, 44.3km

Back to the Šenčur circuit for the TTs. The men and women will complete one lap each in the mixed relay, totalling 44.3km.

All Individual Time-Trials, 22.1km

All the individual time-trials take place on the same day, with everyone completing one 22.1km lap of the same course as all the other events.

UEC European Road Championships 2026 elite favourites

With the European Championships providing a punchy route just after the World Championships, we can look at form from Canada to decipher who will be in the mix in Slovenia. In the men’s road race, look for Remco Evenepoel, who didn’t possess the legs expected of him in the road race after winning gold in the time-trial, plus (probably) Slovenia’s best hope of home glory Primož Roglič, Mads Pedersen, Giulio Ciccone and Juan Ayuso.

Demi Vollering couldn’t complete the solo breakaway she wanted in the fight for rainbows. Could that provide some extra motivation for the defending champion? Looking to dethrone her will be Elisa Longo Borghini and Marlen Reusser, who finished third and fourth in the World Championships. Keep an eye on Paula Blasi, Franzi Koch, Juliette Berthet and Cedrine Kerbaol too.

In the men’s TT, it’s expected that Jakob Söderqvist, Primož Roglič, Mathias Vacek, Bruno Armirail, Ethan Hayter and Callum Thornley should be eyeing the European jersey, with World Champ Evenepoel seemingly skipping this one. Maybe his name is just late to the start list. On the women’s side World Champion Marlen Reusser is the big favourite, with Elisa Longo Borghini and Cédrine Kerbaol likely to be her closest challengers.

How to watch the UEC European Road Championships 2026

The U23 and elite road races and elite individual time-trials will be broadcast on HBO Max in the UK and Eurosport across Europe. In Belgium, it’s VRT 1; in France it’s L’Equipe; in Italy it’s Rai; in Slovenia it’s TV Slovenija 2; in Switzerland it’s SSR (streaming) and RSI LA 2. The UEC will broadcast the junior events on their YouTube channel.
